3: aes
4: ===
5: 
6: Verilog implementation of the [symmetric block cipher AES (NIST FIPS 197)](http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/fips/fips197/fips-197.pdf).
7: 
8: 
9: ## Status ##
10: The core is completed, has been used in several FPGA and ASIC
11: designs. The core is well tested and mature.
12: 
13: 
14: ## Introduction ##
15: 
16: This implementation supports 128 and 256 bit keys. The
17: implementation is iterative and process one 128 block at a time. Blocks
18: are processed on a word level with 4 S-boxes in the data path. The
19: S-boxes for encryption are shared with the key expansion and the core
20: can thus not do key update in parallel with block processing.
21: 
22: The encipher and decipher block processing datapaths are separated and
23: basically self contained given access to a set of round keys and a
24: block. This makes it possible to hard wire the core to only encipher or
25: decipher operation. This allows the synthesis/build tools to optimize
26: away the other functionality which will reduce the size to about
27: 50%. This has been tested to verify that decryption is removed and the
28: core still works.
29: 
30: For cipher modes such as CTR, CCM, CMAC, GCM the decryption
31: functionality in the AES core will never be used and thus the decipher
32: block processing can be removed.
33: 
34: This is a fairly compact implementation. Further reduction could be
35: achived by just having a single S-box. Similarly the performane can be
36: increased by having 8 or even 16 S-boxes which would reduce the number
37: of cycles to two cycles for each round.
38: 
39: 
40: ### Contact information ##
41: 
42: Assured provides customer support including customization, integration
43: and system development related to the core. For more information,
44: please contact [Assured Security
45: Consultants](https://www.assured.se/contact).
46: 
47: 
48: ## Branches ##
49: 
50: There are several branches available that provides different versions of
51: the core. The branches are not planned to be merged into master. The
52: branches available that provides versions of the core are:
53: 
54: 
55: ### on-the-fly-keygen ###
56: 
57: This version of AES implements the key expansion using an on-the-fly
58: mechanism. This allows the initial key expansion to be removed. This
59: saves a number of cycles and also remove almost 1800 registers needed to
60: store the round keys. Note that this version of AES only supports
61: encryption. On-the-fly key generation does not work with
62: decryption. Decryption must be handled by the block cipher mode - for
63: example CTR.
64: 
65: 
66: ### dual-keys ###
67: 
68: This version of AES supports two separate banks of expanded keys to
69: allow fast key switching between two keys. This is useful for example in
70: an AEAD mode with CBC + CMAC implemented using a single AES core.
71: 
72: 
73: ### cmt-sbox ###
74: 
75: An experimental version of the core in which the S-box is implemented
76: using circuit minimized logic functions of a ROM table. The specific
77: table used is
78: [the 113 gate circuit](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/SLP_AES_113.txt) by the [CMT team at Yale](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/CMT.html).
79:

113: ## Core Usage
114: 
115: ### Usage sequence:
116: 1. Load the key to be used by writing to the key register words.
117: 2. Set the key length by writing to the config register.
118: 3. Initialize key expansion by writing a one to the init bit in the control register.
119: 4. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the key expansion has been completed.
120: 5. Write the cleartext block to the block registers.
121: 6. Start block processing by writing a one to the next bit in the control register.
122: 7. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the data block has been processed.
123: 8. Read out the ciphertext block from the result registers.
124:

43:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
44:   // Internal constant and parameter definitions.

48:   parameter CLK_HALF_PERIOD = 1;

51:   // The DUT address map.
52:   parameter ADDR_NAME0       = 8'h00;
53:   parameter ADDR_NAME1       = 8'h01;
54:   parameter ADDR_VERSION     = 8'h02;
55: 
56:   parameter ADDR_CTRL        = 8'h08;
57:   parameter CTRL_INIT_BIT    = 0;
58:   parameter CTRL_NEXT_BIT    = 1;
59:   parameter CTRL_ENCDEC_BIT  = 2;
60:   parameter CTRL_KEYLEN_BIT  = 3;
61: 
62:   parameter ADDR_STATUS      = 8'h09;
63:   parameter STATUS_READY_BIT = 0;

65: 
66:   parameter ADDR_CONFIG      = 8'h0a;
67: 
68:   parameter ADDR_KEY0        = 8'h10;
69:   parameter ADDR_KEY1        = 8'h11;

94:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
95:   // Register and Wire declarations.
96:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
97:   reg [31 : 0]  cycle_ctr;
98:   reg [31 : 0]  error_ctr;
99:   reg [31 : 0]  tc_ctr;
100: 
101:   reg [31 : 0]  read_data;

104:   reg           tb_clk;

106:   reg           tb_cs;
107:   reg           tb_we;

113:   //----------------------------------------------------------------

116:   aes dut(

127:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
128:   // clk_gen
129:   //
130:   // Always running clock generator process.
131:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
132:   always
133:     begin : clk_gen
134:       #CLK_HALF_PERIOD;
135:       tb_clk = !tb_clk;
136:     end // clk_gen
137:

139:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
140:   // sys_monitor()
141:   //
142:   // An always running process that creates a cycle counter and
143:   // conditionally displays information about the DUT.
144:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
145:   always
146:     begin : sys_monitor
147:       cycle_ctr = cycle_ctr + 1;
148: 
149:       #(CLK_PERIOD);
150: 
151:       if (DEBUG)

153:           dump_dut_state();

158:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
159:   // dump_dut_state()
160:   //
161:   // Dump the state of the dump when needed.

165:       $display("cycle: 0x%016x", cycle_ctr);

167:       $display("------------");
168:       $display("ctrl_reg:   init   = 0x%01x, next   = 0x%01x", dut.init_reg, dut.next_reg);
169:       $display("config_reg: encdec = 0x%01x, length = 0x%01x ", dut.encdec_reg, dut.keylen_reg);
170:       $display("");
171: 
172:       $display("block: 0x%08x, 0x%08x, 0x%08x, 0x%08x",
173:                dut.block_reg[0], dut.block_reg[1], dut.block_reg[2], dut.block_reg[3]);
174:       $display("");
175: 
176:     end
177:   endtask // dump_dut_state

180:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
181:   // reset_dut()
182:   //
183:   // Toggle reset to put the DUT into a well known state.
184:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
185:   task reset_dut;
186:     begin
187:       $display("*** Toggle reset.");
188:       tb_reset_n = 0;
189: 
190:       #(2 * CLK_PERIOD);
191:       tb_reset_n = 1;
192:       $display("");

198:   // display_test_results()
199:   //
200:   // Display the accumulated test results.
201:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
202:   task display_test_results;

206:           $display("*** All %02d test cases completed successfully", tc_ctr);

217:   //----------------------------------------------------------------

222:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
223:   task init_sim;

242:   //
243:   // Write the given word to the DUT using the DUT interface.
244:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
245:   task write_word(input [11 : 0] address,
246:                   input [31 : 0] word);
247:     begin
248:       if (DEBUG)
249:         begin
250:           $display("*** Writing 0x%08x to 0x%02x.", word, address);

254:       tb_address = address;

257:       tb_we = 1;

261:     end

266:   // write_block()
267:   //
268:   // Write the given block to the dut.
269:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
270:   task write_block(input [127 : 0] block);
271:     begin
272:       write_word(ADDR_BLOCK0, block[127  :  96]);
273:       write_word(ADDR_BLOCK1, block[95   :  64]);
274:       write_word(ADDR_BLOCK2, block[63   :  32]);
275:       write_word(ADDR_BLOCK3, block[31   :   0]);
276:     end
277:   endtask // write_block

286:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
287:   task read_word(input [11 : 0]  address);
288:     begin

290:       tb_cs = 1;
291:       tb_we = 0;
292:       #(CLK_PERIOD);
293:       read_data = tb_read_data;
294:       tb_cs = 0;
295: 
296:       if (DEBUG)
297:         begin
298:           $display("*** Reading 0x%08x from 0x%02x.", read_data, address);

311:     begin
312:       read_word(ADDR_RESULT0);
313:       result_data[127 : 096] = read_data;
314:       read_word(ADDR_RESULT1);
315:       result_data[095 : 064] = read_data;

330:   task init_key(input [255 : 0] key, input key_length);
331:     begin
332:       if (DEBUG)
333:         begin
334:           $display("key length: 0x%01x", key_length);
335:           $display("Initializing key expansion for key: 0x%016x", key);

340:       write_word(ADDR_KEY2, key[191  : 160]);
341:       write_word(ADDR_KEY3, key[159  : 128]);
342:       write_word(ADDR_KEY4, key[127  :  96]);
343:       write_word(ADDR_KEY5, key[95   :  64]);
344:       write_word(ADDR_KEY6, key[63   :  32]);
345:       write_word(ADDR_KEY7, key[31   :   0]);

347:       if (key_length)
348:         begin
349:           write_word(ADDR_CONFIG, 8'h02);
350:         end
351:       else
352:         begin
353:           write_word(ADDR_CONFIG, 8'h00);
354:         end

356:       write_word(ADDR_CTRL, 8'h01);

358:       #(100 * CLK_PERIOD);
359:     end

370:                                   input [255 : 0] key,
371:                                   input           key_length,
372:                                   input [127 : 0] block,
373:                                   input [127 : 0] expected);

379:       write_block(block);

382:       write_word(ADDR_CONFIG, (8'h00 + (key_length << 1)+ encdec));
383:       write_word(ADDR_CTRL, 8'h02);

385:       #(100 * CLK_PERIOD);

387:       read_result();
